result.topic_en: Euler explains that the variation of an expression is obtained by holding x constant and differentiating only with respect to the auxiliary parameter t, first for functions of x and y alone (Z with dZ = M dx + N dy), and then begins treating expressions involving the derivatives p, q, r.
result.transcription:
38 METHODVM NOVA CALCVLVM
que ipſius $x$. Sumta enim $t$ infinite parua haec aequatio omnes omnino lineas curuas propoſitae proximas in ſe comprehendet atque adeo hanc formam multo generaliorem reddere licet, ita vt pro $y$ functio quaecunque binarum variabilium $x$ et $t$ vſurpari poſſit, dummodo ea ita fuerit comparata, vt poſito $t=0$, prodeat ipſa functio propoſita $y=X$.

7. Pro variatione igitur inuenienda, quantitas $x$ vt conſtans ſpectari ipſius vero $y$ differentiale tantum ex variabilitate ipſius $t$ deſumi debet; vnde ſi expreſſio propoſita fuerit primi generis functio ſcilicet ipſarum $x$ et $y$ tantum, quam littera $Z$ deſignemus; ponamus differentiatione conſueta prodire $M\,dx+N\,dy$ atque nunc pro variatione inuenienda fiat $dx=0$, at loco $dy$ ſcribatur $dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$, quippe quod eſt incrementum ex ſola variabilitate $t$ oriundum. Quo facto variatio quaeſita huius expreſſionis $Z$ erit $=N\,dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$. Quare ſi ipſa variatio ſimili modo per $dt\left(\frac{dZ}{dt}\right)$ indicetur, habebimus $\left(\frac{dZ}{dt}\right)=N\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$.

7. Nunc ad expreſſiones ſecundi generis progrediamur, in quibus quum praeter $x$ et $y$ occurrant quantitates $p$, $q$, $r$ etc. harum variationes quatenus $y$ etiam a variabili $t$ pendet, per legem generalem his formulis exprimentur
$dt\left(\frac{dp}{dt}\right);\; dt\left(\frac{dq}{dt}\right);\; dt\left(\frac{dr}{dt}\right)$ etc.
Quum autem pro ſola variabili $x$, ſit
$p=\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right);\; q=\left(\frac{dp}{dx}\right)=\left(\frac{ddy}{dx^2}\right);$ et $r=\left(\frac{dq}{dx}\right)=\left(\frac{ddp}{dx^2}\right)=\left(\frac{d^3y}{dx^3}\right)$ etc.
erit

items.quote: Sumta enim $t$ infinite parua haec aequatio omnes omnino lineas curuas propoſitae proximas in ſe comprehendet
items.english: For, taking t infinitely small, this equation will comprise within itself absolutely all curves near to the proposed one.

items.quote: Nunc ad expreſſiones ſecundi generis progrediamur, in quibus quum praeter $x$ et $y$ occurrant quantitates $p$, $q$, $r$ etc.
items.english: Now let us proceed to expressions of the second kind, in which, besides x and y, the quantities p, q, r etc. occur.
